item.title: Re: Time: Limited
item.content:encoded:
This collapsible will contain an updated and more in-depth version of the concept.

Massive edit:

Lots of text
Sorry for wall of text

The signals reveal that the canis major dwarf galaxy has been in indefinite quarantine for about a millennia. With the alien race having spent this time keeping the mass from breaching containment and exiting the galaxy.

Further information is received a year later, telling of the origin of the mass. At some point, a signal was triggered by an experimental technology which resulted in a change in the genetic code of 30% of the alien race. This change resulted in the rapid generation of sentient cells that act as a hive mind, think cancer if it had a sense of self. The affected individuals quickly became overwhelmed by the cancerous cells, eventually being entirely consumed. The separate smaller masses sought out one another to grow, as they grew in size, they similarly grew in intellect.

Another year passes before another signal is received (this will be a yearly pattern). The sender expresses immense remorse before divulging information relating to damaging the mass, or at least holding it off. The leaders of the alien species performed many experiments, some far less ethical than others. The spinal fluid of approximately 8% of individuals that die in their sleep contains an anomalous chemical that tears apart the mass on the molecular level. However, the aliens are unsure as to whether or not other species have this same chemical.
In an attempt to neutralise the mass, 50 kilolitres of spinal fluid containing the chemical is dropped onto it. The mass essentially begins melting and makes a direct B line to a megacity on the species home planet. Attempts to stop it are unsuccessful and the mass regenerates. After this, it enters orbit by literally launching itself into space. It adapts to the inhospitable conditions near instantaneously, floating from planet to planet, consuming all life it comes across. A total of 50% of the population had been lost due to the increase in aggression of the mass.

A final effort to prevent the mass from ending the civilisation was made, where a planet the mass had just landed at is encased in a metal alloy. The mass is constantly weakened by continuous railgun fire.
Due to a jam that prevented railgun fire for 20 seconds, the mass was able to tear its containment unit to shreds along with the railgun stations. At this point, the mass had grown sufficiently enough to communicate although in a rudimentary way. It emits a soundwave, saying, “Scaring. Leave.”

The alien race dedicates the rest of its existence to reversing what they believe is their mistake, constantly engaging with the mass and preventing it from leaving the galaxy.
Eventually, the mass adapts, emitting a heatwave that spans the entire galaxy. This heatwave has two effects: Burning any living being to death due to its temperature exceeding 1000 degrees Celsius. Secondly, it converts those exposed into separate instances of the mass, which seek out each other and join the main mass.

The last remnants of the alien race; those housed in underground government facilities, are the ones that sent out the signals. The final signal tells of these last remaining aliens, and how they are sorry for the responsibility that has been placed on the surrounding galaxies.
As the mass reaches 5000 lightyears from earth, it sends out its own signals, which contain a LOT of binary. The translated signals are oddly friendly, stating that it will not bring harm and that it is tired.

Communication is established and the foundation conducts a series of interviews by sending out questions in binary and translating the response. The mass talks of its origin, stating that it does not know how it came to be, only that there was darkness then there was light. It was a child, hungry and afraid, but it is older now and understands that eating causes death. It says that it met a being of machine and flesh, which told the mass a “beautiful message”. The mass has refused to eat since it received the message, choosing to observe and learn. Because it has been starving itself, it is dying. It saw earth and its natural wonders and felt that earth would be a nice final destination. The problem is, of course, that the foundation has been given a very gruesome depiction of this mass, and a large mass of flesh that wiped out an entire civilisation is the easiest to trust.

Essentially, an alien civilisation was wiped out by an eldritch abomination that developed due to their use of experimental technology. They sent out a series of messages to explain what happened, and what threat has been unleashed. The foundation is left with a dilemma though. After the mass expresses a desire to not bring harm but rather to have a peaceful death, the foundation is left having to decide what to trust. Additionally, the mass references "others" in the surrounding galaxies, giving a rather grim reason for why we haven't seen much alien life.

I am also considering having the mass speak of a "father", which will involve some references to Yaldabaoth as a possible reason for the creation of the mass.

item.title: Re: Time: Limited
item.content:encoded:
One thing I learned real early writing on the wiki is that there's a direct trade-off between mystery and amount of story told, and your way too far to one side of that equation.

Regarding your specific idea, you're thinking way, way too small. There's barely anything happening here. If you think about this like a movie, you've got the pre-credits scene, maybe the first act if we're being generous. They detect a signal, do exactly what you would expect them to, and we discover some extremely vague mysterious info about the threat. There's nowhere near enough there for us readers to sink our teeth into, so we aren't going to care enough to fill in the gaps and be scared.

You need to ask yourself at least three really big What next?'s. And I'm not talking small answers, like "the mass is quivering." I'm talking big answer, like "IT GETS HERE" big, or "we discover some really cool or strange unexpected thing about the senders/object/universe" big. That is the scale you're operating on with extraterrestrial SCPs.

Like, in terms of existing SCPs, sometimes the answer to that question was "we find a planet that died as a god was born and all that's left is its massive corpse", or "there was an entire civilisation that was deeply inspired by us and died out, but wanted to thank us", or "ancient humanity slew aliens and destroyers a giant geodesic sphere around Earth," or "the signal led to an invasion of earth so bad that we had to put 055 in 579, told in a dozen successive documents."

(Each of those had mysterious elements as well.)

BIG answers.

Push yourself. A lot. You've barely started.

item.title: Re: Time: Limited
item.content:encoded: To echo some concerns voiced by others, this concept feels very nebulous, pun intended. The concept of "a signal from space warning humanity of impending disaster" has been done several times and while reading this, I kept thinking back to those SCPs, most of which ended up being very long and complex articles. My question is "What makes your idea distinct from other SCPs of the same type?"

item.title: Re: Time: Limited
item.content:encoded:
The first question I have is what is the SCP? You talk about a series of radio transmissions and then an abnormal mass that’s heading towards earth. Your elevator pitch makes me believe that the SCP is the radio signals, however your hook contradicts this and makes me think it is the abnormal mass.

My bad, clarification should have been added. The main anomaly is the signals, the mass is a secondary anomaly I.E. SCP-XXXX-1.

My second question would be how does an astronomer notices this mass? You clearly state that the signals are originating from a galaxy, implying that the foundation can’t narrow it down any further than that; but then you contradict this by saying an astronomer notices a mass exiting the galaxy. For one, the astronomer would barely be able to see the galaxy through the dust plane in the Milky Way, let alone notice a mass heading towards earth, and the mass would have to be absolutely massive for the scientist to see it. And something that big would collapse in on itself due to its own gravitational pull.

This part of your critique, although understandable and will result in adjustments down the line, I feel is not necessarily that big of a problem. The foundation has access to insane technology, both anomalous and non-anomalous, so it isn't too far fetched to believe that they have the means to spot the mass.

I also don't feel that the astronomer noticing the mass exiting the galaxy contradicts anything to do with the signals? There's a stark contrast to invisible radio signals travelling through space and a massive mass exiting a galaxy. I do see your point, however.

As for the mass collapsing in on itself, it can fairly easily be explained as an anomalous effect (although a cheap explanation, it works).

Nice critique! Some parts felt nit picky but there is a good bit of validity.

item.title: Time: Limited
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Horror/Mystery

Elevator Pitch: A series of interstellar radio signals make their way to earth, warning of an impending threat. After the first message, the foundation ensures no other stations can receive the signals.

Central Narrative: After determining the radio signal's origin to be extraterrestrial, the foundation sets about discovering what sent it, why it was sent, where it was sent from, what the threat is, why "protection" is no longer possible, and why it was needed. The answers to these questions are vague, with the threat remaining unknown and the senders of the radio signal also remaining unknown.

However, it is discovered that the signal originated from the Canis Major Dwarf Galaxy, and it is assumed this possible threat the senders were protecting us from likely originated from the same galaxy. This assumption is later confirmed when foundation astronomers discover an abnormal mass exiting the galaxy, with a trajectory towards earth.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The containment procedures for when the mass arrives at earth, which suggest that, if the mass cannot be neutralized and is a threat to all civilisation, then a full planetary evacuation is to commence. My hope is that this will coax the reader into reading deeper.

Additional Notes: Currently N/A. *Edit:* To address critique I will provide some clarification. SCP-XXXX is the designation to the radio signals, SCP-XXXX-1 is the designation to the mass. The mass pulsates rapidly at all times, indicating that it is pushing against its own gravitational pull.

For a more in-depth look refer to my response to Dyslexion and Petrograd.
